correctness.rationale: Equations (1)-(2) exactly reduce the fairness requirements. Elementary convex-hull and pigeonhole arguments prove the subcritical and critical classifications. For any two supported count vectors, equation (3) forces unit exchanges and rational ratios between changed-agent weights; the associated graph has fixed integer count total per connected component, so exact expected shares determine one rational weight vector per support. The n+1 characterization and two-agent congruence formula are derived algebraically. Exact-rational exchange tests and bounded numerical convex-hull tests passed; universal statements rest on proof, not tests.

originality.rationale: The closest binary-chore paper (arXiv:2609.13970 §4) gives a two-agent, two-chore unequal-weight counterexample, rather than an all-m,n feasible-region classification or finite rationality theorem. Deterministic WEF1 existence (arXiv:2301.08090), general weaker transfer-based lottery guarantees (arXiv:2209.03908), and deterministic picking sequence/apportionment work (arXiv:2104.14347) do not logically imply an exact convex-hull characterization. Search results and primary inspection reveal no equivalent theorem; unindexed literature remains a priority risk.

value.rationale: The recent binary-chore paper explicitly motivates the coexistence gap for exact ex-ante WEF versus ex-post WEF1. The theorem identifies a mathematically natural, sharp transition at one chore per agent from a positive-dimensional feasible entitlement region to a finite set of rational exceptional weights; enumerates all 2^n−1 first-supercritical exceptions and all 2m−3 two-agent splits; and provides a structural weight-ratio rigidity lemma with plausible use in constrained allocation and apportionment. Its contribution is not a routine restatement of the motivating two-chore counterexample.
